title: Cortex: the Activity Monitor for the AI era
excerpt: Cortex groups 1,000 Mac processes into the apps you run, keeps 30 days of history, and shows what your Neural Engine and local AI models are doing.
content_html:
System monitor for macOS

Cortex turns a thousand processes into the sixty apps you actually run, remembers the last 30 days, and shows what your Neural Engine and local models are doing. Everything stays on your Mac.

One-time purchase · macOS 15 or later · Built for Apple Silicon

Metric tiles are decorative, not real data.

  • 1,000 → 60Processes grouped into apps
  • 30 daysOf history for every app
  • 0Accounts, trackers or analytics
  • 1Payment. No subscription

Apps, not processes

See sixty apps, not a thousand processes.

Activity Monitor lists what the system sees: helpers, renderers, agents and daemons. Cortex counts each one under the app it belongs to, so a slow Mac has a name you recognise. Expand any app when you want the detail.

Built for Apple Silicon AI

Goes further on the hardware that runs your models.

Neural Engine power, local model memory, and an honest answer to "can I run this?". No other system monitor covers this much of Apple Silicon.

Apple Silicon

Neural Engine

See Neural Engine power and estimated load next to CPU, GPU and DRAM, and which apps hold Neural Engine memory.

Local AI

Local AI workloads

Cortex detects Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, ComfyUI and MLX or PyTorch processes, and shows the models they have loaded.

Can I run this model?

Model Fit Advisor

Pick the parameters, quantization and context length. Cortex compares the model with your free unified memory and the GPU memory limit.

On-device assistant

Ask Cortex

Ask "Why is my Mac slow?" or "What drained my battery?" and get an answer from your own data, on your Mac.

Try asking

  • What drained my battery?
  • Why are the fans loud?
  • Which dev servers are idle?

Answers are computed on your Mac with Apple's on-device models. Needs macOS 26 and Apple Intelligence; otherwise a built-in assistant answers.

See every feature

Everything else

The rest of what your Mac is doing.

  • 30 days of history

    Every metric, for every app, kept for 30 days. Find out what happened while you were away.

  • Smart alerts

    Cortex learns what is normal for each app at each hour of the week, and tells you when something is not.

  • CPU, core by core

    Performance cores and efficiency cores, shown separately, so you know which kind of work is running.

  • Memory that makes sense

    Memory pressure, swap and a clear breakdown of where your unified memory went.

  • Disk and network

    Reads, writes and traffic per app, so you can see who is hammering the disk or the network.

  • Battery, temperatures and fans

    Battery health, cycle count and power draw, with temperatures and fan speeds alongside.

  • Silicon Probe

    A short benchmark of the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine, tracked over time on your own Mac.

  • Projects

    Dev servers on listening ports, grouped by project. Find the one you forgot three days ago.

  • Daily digest

    Each evening, a short summary of your Mac's day.

See every feature

Privacy

What happens on your Mac stays on your Mac.

Cortex sees everything your Mac does, so it keeps all of it local. No account. No analytics. No telemetry. Ask Cortex runs on device.

  • No account
  • No analytics
  • No telemetry
  • On-device AI

Read the privacy policy

The only two requests Cortex makes

  1. 1Update checkLooks for a new version of Cortex.
  2. 2License checkSends your license key, your Mac’s name and an anonymous device ID.

Everything else, including 30 days of history and every Ask Cortex answer, stays on your Mac.

Pricing

Pay once. Keep it.

No subscription and no trial. Buy it, activate it, and it keeps working, even offline.

Is Cortex on the Mac App Store?

No. Cortex needs to read other apps’ processes, which the App Store sandbox does not allow. It is distributed directly, signed and notarized by Apple.

Does it work on Intel Macs?

Yes. Cortex is built for Apple Silicon, and Intel Macs are supported with fewer metrics: there is no Neural Engine and no power data. It needs macOS 15 Sequoia or later.

How much does it cost?

$5, once, for the first 100 licenses. After that the price is $19. There is no subscription and no trial. Every future update is included, for life. See the update policy.

Can I buy Cortex for more than one Mac?

Yes. Pick 1, 2, 5, 10 or 20 licenses on the pricing card. Each license is $5 and activates Cortex on one Mac at a time, so 5 licenses cover 5 Macs. You pay once, as with a single license.

How do I move my license to a new Mac?

One license covers one Mac at a time. On the old Mac, open Cortex › Settings › License and choose Deactivate This Mac. Then enter your key on the new Mac.

If you enter the key on a second Mac first, Cortex tells you which Mac has it and when that Mac was last used.

Is my data uploaded?

No. Your metrics, history and Ask Cortex conversations stay on your Mac. Cortex makes only two kinds of network request: the update check and the license check. There is no telemetry.

Know what your Mac is doing.

Does it work on Intel Macs?

是的。 Cortex is built for Apple Silicon, and Intel Macs are supported with fewer metrics: there is no Neural Engine and no power data. It needs macOS 15 Sequoia or later.

How much does it cost?

$5, once, for the first 100 licenses. After that the price is $19. There is no subscription and no trial. Every future update is included, for life. See the update policy.

Can I buy Cortex for more than one Mac?

是的。 Pick 1, 2, 5, 10 or 20 licenses on the pricing card. Each license is $5 and activates Cortex on one Mac at a time, so 5 licenses cover 5 Macs. You pay once, as with a single license.

How do I move my license to a new Mac?

One license covers one Mac at a time. On the old Mac, open Cortex › Settings › License and choose Deactivate This Mac. Then enter your key on the new Mac.

If you enter the key on a second Mac first, Cortex tells you which Mac has it and when that Mac was last used.

Is my data uploaded?

No. Your metrics, history and Ask Cortex conversations stay on your Mac. Cortex makes only two kinds of network request: the update check and the license check. There is no telemetry.
